selection_rationale: Candidate cnd-2026-004 (verifier taxonomy + open benchmark) best matches the autonomy, novelty, and feasibility constraints: it requires no human-in-the-loop scoring, directly addresses a documented methodology/tooling gap, and reviewers rated its novelty highest while providing actionable repairs that preserve full automation and reproducibility.
unresolved_uncertainties: Public-corpus representativeness given vendor/privacy limits for benchmark curation
Risk that taxonomy axes oversimplify hybrid verifier behaviors and fail to predict detectability for some failure classes
Potential bias in injected failures (engineered vs naturalistic) altering measured detector coverage
Community adoption dependent on ease of reproducing oracle implementations and documentation quality
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Limit corpus to provably public, non-sensitive sources; document provenance and anonymization steps for every item.
Define taxonomy axes as precise, machine-readable descriptors and provide mapping rules with concrete examples tying attributes to verifier implementations.
Design and document an adversary-aware injection protocol balancing naturalistic and engineered failure modes; publish injection scripts and fixed seeds.
Provide containerized exemplar oracle implementations (Docker), unit tests, and a small end-to-end replication script; include a reproducibility checklist and packaging instructions.
